incidents.victim: NetNut / Popa residential proxy botnet (millions of consumer smart TVs and streaming boxes)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — residential proxy botnet operator
incidents.vector: Malicious SDKs bundled into consumer-device apps silently conscripted smart TVs and streaming boxes into an always-on residential proxy network rented out to relay abusive traffic.
incidents.impact: FBI, IRS-CI, Google and Lumen disrupted the ~2M-device network that had powered password-spray, scraping, ad fraud and account takeover for 316 distinct threat clusters; domains seized and accounts disabled.

incidents.victim: Taiwanese politicians, academics, journalists and civil society
incidents.vector: Operators impersonated international journalists using rented LINE accounts to build trust, then lured targets into downloading malware disguised as encrypted communications software.
incidents.impact: Broad phishing-and-espionage campaign (100+ malicious domains over nine months) aimed at stealing credentials and compromising devices of prominent Taiwanese figures; Taiwan charged two businessmen for supplying the LINE accounts.

incidents.victim: Nayax Ltd. (payments / vending technology, Israel)
incidents.vector: Unusual activity was detected in a cloud account belonging to a Nayax subsidiary and was blocked and contained.
incidents.impact: Cloud-account intrusion under investigation with US and Israeli law enforcement; scope of affected data still being determined. Company states production and core systems were unaffected.

incidents.victim: Unnamed global enterprise (large AWS cloud environment)
incidents.vector: A lone attacker obtained an AWS access key via an internet-facing application, then used agentic AI workflows to chain weaknesses across app services, source repos, CI/CD pipelines and data stores.
incidents.impact: Compromised the AWS environment in roughly 72 hours, harvested secrets, exfiltrated data and staged reversible disruptive actions (blocking S3, zeroing ECS, purging queues) to extort the victim, per Sygnia research.

incidents.victim: U.S. and Canadian universities (physics and engineering departments)
incidents.vector: Phishing emails chained two Roundcube webmail vulnerabilities (CVE-2024-42009 and CVE-2025-49113) to run JavaScript on the mail server, then dropped webshells and backdoors.
incidents.impact: Attackers gained persistent access and stole credentials from professors and administrators with national-security links; fewer than ten victims confirmed but dozens assessed as impacted.

incidents.victim: Consumers and small/medium businesses (U.S. and EU)
incidents.vector: Malvertising lured victims to fake cracked-software installers that deployed a Go-based loader dropping the Vidar stealer and the XMRig Monero miner, using a forged code-signing certificate and file-size inflation to evade detection.
incidents.impact: Steals browser credentials, cookies and crypto wallets and mines Monero on victim machines; part of a concurrent Vidar/Lumma stealer campaign analyzed by Unit 42.

incidents.victim: High-value targets reached via compromised Ruckus, ASUS and IoT devices
incidents.vector: Exploited known vulnerabilities in unpatched Ruckus and ASUS routers, then deployed custom Linux backdoors to enroll devices into operational relay (ORB) proxy networks.
incidents.impact: Builds and expands ORB proxy networks that secondary Chinese espionage groups use to obfuscate attacks on high-value targets; Cisco Talos observed continued malware development.

incidents.victim: KDDI (email platform serving five Japanese ISPs)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in third-party software used by an email platform KDDI operates for internet service providers.
incidents.impact: Exposed more than 12.2 million customer email addresses and 7.6 million passwords; the flaw was patched and mandatory password resets are underway.

incidents.victim: Microsoft 365 users in finance, HR and logistics roles (incl. a U.S. life-sciences company)
incidents.vector: Vendor-impersonation invoice-fraud phishing lured victims through look-alike SharePoint tenants into Microsoft OAuth device-code authentication, capturing tokens and Primary Refresh Tokens to bypass MFA.
incidents.impact: Enables full mailbox access, business email compromise and document theft that persists across password resets; Talos recovered live lures sent against a U.S. life-sciences company.

incidents.victim: Aflac (Japan branch)
incidents.vector: Undisclosed intrusion into the Japanese branch's systems.
incidents.impact: Customer data stolen affecting more than 4.38 million customers; follows a separate Aflac breach disclosed a year earlier.

incidents.victim: Central Bank of Libya
incidents.vector: Network breach traced to an intrusion roughly three weeks earlier, followed by publication of stolen files.
incidents.impact: Files allegedly taken from the central bank's network were leaked on the dark web by the Qilin ransomware group; Libyan authorities are investigating.

incidents.victim: Nissan North America
incidents.vector: Breach linked to the wave of exploitation of a zero-day vulnerability in Oracle PeopleSoft.
incidents.impact: Nissan North America disclosed a security breach tied to the Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day hacking campaign.

incidents.victim: Browser users (2.6M+ downloads across Edge, Chrome and Firefox)
incidents.vector: 119 malicious extensions with genuine functionality delivered payloads several days after install, using steganography to hide command-and-control instructions.
incidents.impact: Stole credentials, backdoored browsers and ran ad/search affiliate fraud; Microsoft disrupted the 'StegoAd' operation and removed the extensions.

incidents.victim: U.S. and allied government officials, military, journalists and Ukrainian officials
incidents.vector: Phishing impersonating commercial messaging-app (Signal) support accounts tricked high-value targets into sharing verification codes, PINs and Backup Recovery Keys.
incidents.impact: Actors compromised individual messaging accounts, gaining access to full message history and enabling durable account takeover; FBI/CISA issued an updated joint advisory with new phishing samples.

incidents.victim: John Bolton (former U.S. National Security Advisor) — personal email account
incidents.vector: Iran-linked actor hacked Bolton's personal email account, which contained classified national-defense information he had improperly transmitted.
incidents.impact: A foreign adversary accessed TOP SECRET/SCI material including military plans and covert operations; Bolton pleaded guilty to violating the Espionage Act.

incidents.victim: Japan Self-Defense Forces (classified networks)
incidents.vector: USB drives infected with Chinese malware were connected to classified networks.
incidents.impact: Possible compromise of classified networks kept quiet for nearly a year; Japan is notifying NATO partners of a potential leak.

incidents.victim: Internet-exposed Fortinet, Sophos and MSSQL services (tens of thousands of devices)
incidents.vector: Internet-wide password spraying against Fortinet, Sophos and MSSQL services, followed by privilege-escalation exploits, device-configuration extraction and offline password cracking.
incidents.impact: Credentials harvested from tens of thousands of edge devices and offered for sale by an initial access broker ('FortiBleed'), enabling persistent high-privilege administrative access.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian government and military; entities linked to Italian foreign policy
incidents.vector: Deployment of a multi-component .NET backdoor ('STOCKSTAY') disguised as benign applications, communicating with command-and-control over encrypted WebSocket channels.
incidents.impact: Enables file theft, screen capture, registry manipulation and command execution for long-running cyber espionage; Google ties the tooling to the long-running FSB-attributed Turla operation.

incidents.victim: Southeast Asian government and state-owned energy infrastructure (10+ organizations)
incidents.vector: Exploited web applications to plant ASPX web shells, then used VPN tooling, credential dumping and a bespoke .NET backdoor for tunneling and data theft.
incidents.impact: Compromised at least ten organizations, exfiltrated database contents and web-server source code, and breached two state-owned critical energy infrastructure entities (Oct–Dec 2025).

incidents.victim: Transport for London; SSM Health and Sutter Health (U.S. healthcare)
incidents.vector: Voice/SMS phishing and SIM-swapping to steal employee credentials and MFA codes, enabling network intrusion and extortion.
incidents.impact: Two 'Scattered Spider' members pleaded guilty over the Aug 2024 attack that crippled Transport for London and intrusions at U.S. healthcare providers; a related U.S. indictment alleges 120 intrusions and at least $115M in ransoms.

incidents.victim: Polymarket (prediction market)
incidents.vector: Attackers breached a third-party vendor and loaded malicious code onto Polymarket's website.
incidents.impact: Roughly $3 million was stolen before detection; Polymarket pledged to reimburse affected users.

incidents.victim: SecondFi (cryptocurrency platform)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a bug in the platform's web-wallet generation software.
incidents.impact: More than $2.4 million in customer assets stolen; the platform entered maintenance mode and pledged refunds.

incidents.victim: Nidec Corporation
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack that forced the company to take its entire IT network offline.
incidents.impact: A new ransomware group ('BLackField') demanded a $2 million ransom; Nidec took its full IT network offline, having also been hit by ransomware in late 2024.

incidents.victim: Bajaj Auto (India) — engineering subsidiary
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack affecting an engineering and research subsidiary.
incidents.impact: Operations of the subsidiary were disrupted; the incident was disclosed to Indian market authorities.

incidents.victim: Klue customers (~20 SaaS companies incl. Deel, Snyk, Jamf, Tanium, Recorded Future)
incidents.vector: Attackers breached Klue's network, stole OAuth tokens from customer accounts and accessed their connected Salesforce integrations.
incidents.impact: Supply-chain breach with a victim list approaching 20 companies; sensitive data was stolen from customers' Salesforce environments.

incidents.victim: AdaptHealth (U.S. medical equipment maker)
incidents.vector: Intruder accessed patient data and internal documents in a cloud-based platform; timeline matches the Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day exploitation spree.
incidents.impact: Patient data and internal documents were accessed; the breach was disclosed to the SEC and investors.

incidents.victim: DHS Homeland Security Information Network (HSIN)
incidents.vector: Intrusion targeting HSIN servers and a connected SharePoint system.
incidents.impact: Hackers breached a DHS network used to share sensitive data with federal, state, local and industry partners between late May and early June; the scope of stolen data is unknown.

incidents.victim: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC)
incidents.vector: Network intrusion attributed to the 'ShinyHunters' data-extortion group.
incidents.impact: NAIC suspended risk designations for insurers and credit-rating agencies paused data sharing to avoid exposure; the intruders were later evicted and operations restored.

incidents.victim: Tata Electronics (Apple supplier)
incidents.vector: Data-extortion breach; the group leaked documents after the company refused to pay.
incidents.impact: The 'World Leaks' group leaked 200,000 documents, including images of unreleased iPhone components.

incidents.victim: Pi Mobile (Taiwanese mobile operator)
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack on the telecom operator's network.
incidents.impact: The operator was hacked and extorted by a new ransomware operation ('Settra'); it says its mobile-payments platform was unaffected and Taiwan opened an investigation.

incidents.victim: Grand Line (Russian construction company)
incidents.vector: Destructive intrusion that wiped servers, workstations, virtual machines and backups, combined with data theft.
incidents.impact: Attackers claimed wiping 3,000 servers/workstations and 700 VMs, deleting all backups and stealing 650+ TB of documents from one of Russia's largest construction firms.

incidents.victim: Fox Rothschild (U.S. law firm)
incidents.vector: Network breach in May 2026 followed by an extortion demand.
incidents.impact: The 'Silent Ransom Group' breached the firm, which refused to pay the ransom.
